Bardejov Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Tehelná 2, Slovakia

Not demolished. Bardejov's Jewish presence is first documented in 1599; Jews were evicted from the city from 1631 and only returned at the start of the 18th century, by which point this cemetery already existed, its oldest tombstone dated 1796. A Hevra Kadisha was founded in 1808, and the Great Synagogue built in the 1830s. Rabbi Haim Abraham Orenstein, author of Divrei Avraham, served from 1856 to 1871; in 1874, Moshe Halberstamm, grandson of the Admor of Sanz, documented at length elsewhere in this collection, became rabbi. The Jewish population reached 2,441 (8.7 percent) by the start of WWII; in September 1940, about 200 Jews were deported to labor camps, and the rest were later sent to various camps and cities in Poland, including Auschwitz. After more than 260 years of continuous Jewish presence, the last Jew of Bardejov died in 2005, and none remain today.
